description: Imposes a hand-written breakpoint envelope on a soundfile, TIME-SCALING the envelope to the sound's duration first - the envelope's time axis is relative, so one shape file fits any input length. Verified: an envelope peaking at time 1 of a 0-4 axis put its gain peak at 0.25 s on a 1 s input and 0.5 s on a 2 s input (both = dur/4); duration static and exact on both. The envelope file is a plain text time/value list (the pre-output aux slot, written with write_data_file()): at least 2 pairs required ('ERROR: Not enough data in brkpnt file <name>' verbatim on a 1-pair file); values above 1 are accepted and AMPLIFY (verified peak gain 1.23 from a value-2.0 envelope). Multiplicative onto the existing envelope, like envel impose. No numeric parameters. Deterministic; stereo accepted.
musical_use: The proportional-shape sibling of envel impose mode 3: where impose reads envelope times literally, scaled stretches your shape to WHATEVER the input's length is - write 'quiet-loud-quiet' once between times 0 and 1 (or 0 and 1000, the units are arbitrary) and apply the same dramatic arc to a 0.5 s grain and a 30 s drone. Ideal for batch-shaping heterogeneous material into a family (same relative dynamics = perceived relatedness), for building crescendo/decay archetypes, or for tremolo-like ripples whose count stays fixed while their rate adapts to each file's length. Values >1 amplify, so shapes can both carve and boost; keep the product of source peak and envelope value under 1.0 to avoid hot floats. For absolute-time envelopes use envel impose/replace; for envelope capture from audio use envel extract.

envelope.description: Text breakpoint file: 'time value' pairs, one per line, times ascending, RELATIVE time axis (stretched to the input duration; units arbitrary). Minimum 2 pairs ('Not enough data in brkpnt file' refused verbatim). Values are gain multipliers; 0-1 shapes, >1 amplifies (accepted, verified). Occupies CDP's argv slot BETWEEN the input and output ('envel scaled infile brkfile outfile') - the position: pre_output layout. Write it with write_data_file(); .txt names work (this build's brkfile readers accept any non-reserved extension).

examples.description: One arch shape for any file length.
examples.expected_use:
First: write_data_file('arch.txt', '0 0
1 1
4 0
'). Peak lands at 1/4 of ANY input's duration (verified at 1 s and 2 s). Output duration = input duration.

examples.description: Fixed-count tremolo ripple that adapts its rate to the file.
examples.expected_use: An 8-hump 0/1 alternation over times 0-8 gives exactly 8 pulses on every input, fast on short files, slow on long ones.

known_issues: The envelope's time axis is RELATIVE (scaled to the input duration) - this is the defining difference from envel impose mode 3, whose breakpoint times are absolute seconds. Same shape, different contract.
Envelope values above 1.0 amplify without clamping (float output can exceed full scale); the engine's post-run verification will flag silence but not clipping - stage headroom yourself.
Fewer than 2 breakpoint pairs refuses 'ERROR: Not enough data in brkpnt file <name>' (exit 255).
The transfer is multiplicative onto the source's own dynamics (like envel impose), not a replacement - use envel replace semantics via execute() if the source envelope must be erased first.
Deterministic; duration static and exact at both probed input durations; stereo accepted.
